title: Impact of COPS Grant on Violent Crime Rates

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy

**Method: Difference-in-Differences (DID)**

The data structure clearly supports a DID design: we have municipalities that are treated (received COPS grants) and untreated (did not receive grants), observed in pre- and post-treatment periods. The `treat_x_post` interaction term is the DID estimator.

**Key Assumption:** Parallel trends — in the absence of the COPS grant, treated and control municipalities would have experienced the same trends in log violent crime rates. This is plausible if grant allocation is not driven by differential pre-existing crime trends (though we should check this).

**Estimating equation:**
$$y_{it} = \alpha + \beta_1 \cdot \text{treated}_i + \beta_2 \cdot \text{post}_t + \delta \cdot \text{treat\_x\_post}_{it} + \epsilon_{it}$$

where $\delta$ is the causal effect of COPS grant receipt on log violent crime rates.

## 2. R Code

```r
# Load necessary libraries
library(lmtest)
library(sandwich)
library(fixest)

# Read data
df <- read.csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s46_data.csv")

# ---- Explore the data ----
cat("=== Data Overview ===\n")
cat("Dimensions:", nrow(df), "rows,", ncol(df), "columns\n")
cat("Periods:", sort(unique(df$period)), "\n")
cat("Number of units:", length(unique(df$unit_id)), "\n")
cat("Treated units:", sum(df$treated[!duplicated(df$unit_id)]), "\n")
cat("Control units:", sum(!df$treated[!duplicated(df$unit_id)]), "\n\n")

# Summary statistics by group
cat("=== Mean outcomes by group ===\n")
tapply(df$y, list(Treated = df$treated, Post = df$post), mean) |> print()
cat("\n")

# ---- Main DID Estimation ----
# Model 1: Basic OLS DID
did_basic <- lm(y ~ treated + post + treat_x_post, data = df)
cat("=== Model 1: Basic DID (OLS) ===\n")
summary(did_basic)

# Robust standard errors
cat("\n=== Model 1: With robust (HC1) standard errors ===\n")
coeftest(did_basic, vcov = vcovHC(did_basic, type = "HC1")) |> print()

# ---- Model 2: DID with unit and time fixed effects ----
cat("\n=== Model 2: Two-way Fixed Effects (Unit + Period FE) ===\n")
did_twfe <- feols(y ~ treat_x_post | unit_id + period, data = df)
summary(did_twfe)

# ---- Model 3: Clustered standard errors at unit level ----
cat("\n=== Model 3: TWFE with clustered SEs at unit level ===\n")
did_clustered <- feols(y ~ treat_x_post | unit_id + period, 
                       cluster = ~unit_id, data = df)
summary(did_clustered)

# ---- Robustness Check 1: Pre-trend analysis ----
cat("\n=== Robustness: Pre-period means by group ===\n")
pre_data <- df[df$post == 0, ]
pre_means <- aggregate(y ~ treated + period, data = pre_data, FUN = mean)
cat("Pre-period means:\n")
print(pre_means)

# If multiple pre-periods, test for differential pre-trends
if (length(unique(pre_data$period)) > 1) {
  pre_trend_test <- lm(y ~ treated * factor(period), data = pre_data)
  cat("\nPre-trend interaction test:\n")
  summary(pre_trend_test)
}

# ---- Robustness Check 2: Event study (if multiple periods) ----
n_periods <- length(unique(df$period))
if (n_periods > 2) {
  cat("\n=== Event Study Specification ===\n")
  df$period_factor <- factor(df$period)
  # Use first period as reference
  ref_period <- min(df$period[df$post == 1]) - 1
  df$period_factor <- relevel(df$period_factor, ref = as.character(ref_period))
  event_study <- feols(y ~ i(period, treated, ref = ref_period) | unit_id + period, 
                       cluster = ~unit_id, data = df)
  summary(event_study)
}

# ---- Print main result clearly ----
cat("\n========================================\n")
cat("       MAIN DID RESULT SUMMARY\n")
cat("========================================\n")
delta <- coef(did_basic)["treat_x_post"]
cat(sprintf("DID Estimate (treat_x_post): %.4f\n", delta))
cat(sprintf("Interpretation: COPS grant receipt is associated with a %.2f%% change\n", 
            delta * 100))
cat("in violent crime rates.\n")
cat("========================================\n")
```

## 3. Expected Findings

**Expected sign:** Negative. COPS grants fund police hiring, which should increase police presence and deterrence, thereby reducing violent crime rates.

**Expected magnitude:** Since the outcome is in logs, the DID coefficient represents an approximate percentage change. I expect a coefficient around **-0.2 to -0.5**, implying a 20–50% reduction in violent crime rates. The literature on COPS grants (e.g., Evans & Owens, 2007) finds meaningful but modest reductions in crime from additional police, so a moderate negative effect is consistent with prior evidence.

**Robustness:** If the parallel trends assumption holds, pre-period interaction terms should be statistically insignificant. The TWFE and clustered SE results should be qualitatively similar to the basic OLS DID but with potentially larger standard errors.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Compare changes in violent crime rates between municipalities that received the grant and those that did not, before and after the grant allocation.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: The analysis reveals a positive effect of the COPS grant on the violent crime rate.
